title: Vertical and horizontal scaling: the limit of each

videos.script: A system scales when the next thousand users cost about what the last thousand did. {{definition}} This course is about what happens when that stops being true, and about seeing it happen. First you build a lab on your own computer: a small box office for concerts, a database behind it, and a program that sends it load. {{lab}} Then you measure it. One process on one processor sells about a hundred and fifty tickets a second. {{baseline}} Give it more processors and the number climbs. That is vertical scaling, and it ends where the biggest machine ends. {{vertical}} Run three copies behind a load balancer and the number climbs again. That is horizontal scaling, and it only works because the copies share nothing. {{horizontal}} Then you point every buyer at the same concert. Three copies sell no more than one did, because every sale waits for one row in the database. {{hotrow}} That row is where the rest of the course begins.
